current_evidence: The council's 'Making a planning application' page links only this 'Local Requirements List' PDF, and the document text is dated 'November 2025' and says it replaces the 2023 version of the checklist.

issues.detail: The reference row says 'Joint / shared list' is null and the list is 'council-specific (no shared list identified)'. The document is in fact a joint list for Malvern Hills and Wychavon District Councils (a shared planning service, under the South Worcestershire Development Plan).
issues.evidence: Title: 'Local Area Planning Application Validation Requirements List' (Malvern Hills and Wychavon District Councils); CIL text: 'Malvern Hills and Wychavon District Council has adopted a Community Infrastructure Charging Levy'

issues.detail: Water Management Statement is missing from every app_type row. The 2025 list requires it for all applications that drain foul or surface water, and the planning page says it should be submitted with householder applications. It appears only as a 'Submission rules' tab item and is never mapped to Householder or Full planning.
issues.evidence: 'Water Management Statement ... For all applications that result in waste or surface water to be drained.' Planning page: 'The Water Management Statement should be submitted with householder planning applications.'

issues.detail: The Householder row lists only the Design and Access Statement. It leaves out the householder biodiversity checklist that the planning page asks for, and leaves out the Heritage Statement for householder works affecting heritage assets (the list says 'any planning application').
issues.evidence: Planning page: for householder applications 'complete this checklist and include it with your application'; Heritage Statement: 'Any planning application or application seeking listed building consent which affects the significance of a designated or non-designated heritage asset'

issues.detail: Glint and Glare Assessment is missing. Its trigger is all planning applications proposing solar farms.
issues.evidence: 'Glint and Glare Assessment ... With all planning applications proposing solar farms.'

issues.detail: Existing Employment Sites Assessment is missing. Its trigger is a change of use or redevelopment of B1/B2/B8 premises (1,000 sq m net or more in urban areas) or of rural employment, tourism or leisure premises to non-employment uses, with 12 months of marketing evidence.
issues.evidence: 'An assessment will be required with:- all planning applications proposing change of use/re-development of existing B1, B2 and/or B8 use class premises'

issues.detail: Replacement Rural Dwellings Statement is missing. Its trigger is an application to demolish an existing dwelling in open countryside and replace it.
issues.evidence: 'With all applications proposing the demolition of an existing dwelling in open countryside and its replacement with a new dwelling.'

issues.detail: Heritage Statement appears only under Listed building consent. The list also requires it for any planning application affecting a designated or non-designated heritage asset or its setting, so it is missing from Full planning, Householder and Outline.
issues.evidence: 'Any planning application or application seeking listed building consent which affects the significance of a designated or non - designated heritage asset, including its setting.'

issues.detail: The 'Sequential / Exception Test (flood)' row is mislabelled. Its excerpt is the town-centre retail sequential test from the Retail and Centres Impact Assessment section, not the flood sequential or exception test. Retail and Centres Impact Assessment (main town centre uses outside SWDP10 centres, or retail/leisure over 1,000 sq m net) therefore has no correctly named row.
issues.evidence: Excerpt: 'with the sequential test as set out under para. 87 of the NPPF ... for all retail or leisure development of over 1,000 sq metres'; source heading: 'Retail and Centres Impact Assessment'

issues.detail: The 'Agricultural / rural workers' dwelling appraisal' row reuses the Agricultural Land Classification excerpt word for word, so it has no trigger of its own. The real trigger for the Rural Workers' Dwelling Justification is a rural dwelling justified by an agricultural, forestry or other rural business need. The ALC row also lacks its thresholds: loss of over 5 ha of agricultural land or 2 ha of BMV land, and large greenfield solar farms.
issues.evidence: 'Where an application is made for a dwelling in a rural location justified by its association with an agricultural/forestry or other rural business need'; 'any development that results in the loss of over 5 hectares of land currently in agricultural use or 2 hectares BMV'

issues.detail: The Design and Access Statement and Environmental Statement (EIA) rows under Full planning both carry the same fragment about CIL adoption. That fragment states no trigger for either document.
issues.evidence: Excerpt for both: 'link: and Environmental Impact Assessment (see advice on It should be noted that Malvern Hills and Wychavon District Council has adopted a Community Infrastructure Charging Levy.'

issues.detail: The Travel Plan row copies the Transport Assessment excerpt, so its own threshold is lost. A Travel Plan is required for all major development (10 or more dwellings or over 1,000 sq m non-residential floorspace) and for any proposal with a Transport Assessment.
issues.evidence: 'Travel Plans will be required for all major development ... 10 or more dwellings or more than 1,000 sq. metres of non-residential building floorspace'

issues.detail: The Noise Impact Assessment trigger is a cut-off fragment about the PPG and gives no trigger. The real trigger is new noise-generating development near noise-sensitive uses, or new noise-sensitive development (housing, hotels, hostels) in noisy areas. The Viability Assessment trigger is also a 4-word fragment: 'reasoning (e.g. a Viability Assessment).'
issues.evidence: 'Noise Assessments will be required ... new development that may create additional noise in areas where noise sensitive development already exists'

issues.detail: Several rows are mislabelled. 'Floor plans / Elevations (existing and proposed)' is actually the Street-scene Elevations requirement, which duplicates the separate street-scene row. 'Schedule of works (listed building)' is actually the schedule required with a Structural Survey for converting a rural building, not a listed-building schedule.
issues.evidence: Floor plans row excerpt begins '- Street-scene Elevations Policy Drivers ...'; Schedule row: 'a full schedule of works (with plans) will be required to clearly explain and illustrate the works required to carry out the proposed conversion.'

issues.detail: Three items are placed under Change of use - prior approval although their triggers refer to planning applications: Flood Risk Assessment, the rural buildings Marketing Report (whose source is the superseded 2021 list) and Structural Survey. The only explicit prior-approval reference in the list is Telecommunications (Part 24). The Structural Survey trigger names 'planning application/applications for listed building consent' and 'a planning application proposing the conversion of an existing rural building'.
issues.evidence: Marketing Report: 'For applications proposing the conversion of a rural building last used for B1, B2, B8 ...'; Structural Survey: 'a planning application proposing the conversion of an existing rural building'

issues.detail: About 30 rows are tagged 'INFERRED ... placed under Full planning' (for example Air Quality, Energy Statement, HIA, Lighting and LVIA). Many of these also apply to Outline and other applications, and some have explicit thresholds Grokbot did not use. For example, LVIA applies to 'development other than householder development in National Landscapes', and the Energy Statement applies to new development over 100 sq m or one or more dwellings. Outline gets only the DAS.
issues.evidence: LVIA: 'development other than householder development in National Landscapes'; Energy: 'new development over 100 sq. metres gross, or one or more dwellings'

issues.detail: Some rows and tab items are sourced from the superseded 2021 'Local Area Requirements List Merged 2021.pdf' rather than the November 2025 list: the Planning Obligations Heads of Terms row, the Marketing row under prior approval, and several 'Submission rules' items. This creates a duplicate street-scene item, one from 2021 and one from 2025.

Several tab items are not requirements. 'Policy-driven requirements' contains a list of contact centre and library addresses (Pershore Civic Centre, Droitwich Spa Library, etc.) taken from a local listed buildings SPD page. 'Submission rules' includes a note on the national fee rise (1 April 2026), links to the planning application guide and the Local Requirements List, and garbled fragments ('Further advice ... b13554-local-auth-guidance-100326.pdf 32.' and 'CIL Charging Structure ... Reg 123 Final Verison - MHDC.pdf ...').
issues.evidence: Tab item: 'Pershore Civic Centre, Queen Elizabeth Drive Droitwich Spa Community Contact Centre ... Contact us:'

summary: Grokbot's link is the current November 2025 Malvern Hills and Wychavon joint list, and the date is right, but the workbook misses that the list is joint. The extraction misses several requirements (Water Management Statement for all applications including householders, Glint and Glare, Existing Employment Sites, Replacement Rural Dwellings, Retail Impact), mislabels or copies triggers between rows, and mixes in the superseded 2021 list and contact or fee boilerplate.

withdrawn_issues.detail: The Intelligently Green declaration is folded into the Water Management 'Submission rules' item as if it were required. The planning page says submission is entirely voluntary.
withdrawn_issues.grok_comment: The Intelligently Green text is indeed appended to the Water Management 'Submission rules' item, but the captured text itself says "Applicants are invited to submit a statement", so it is not presented as mandatory.
withdrawn_issues.claude_response: Accepted. The captured text says applicants are "invited", so it is not presented as mandatory.
